Preface

It came to my attention, in a post made by @KidQuantum, that the solution I've made doesn't work in Internet Explorer. I've come across this quirk before and I suspect that it's because IE prioritizes and cascades property values from the main selectors into psuedo-elements like :after. This means that the visibility: hidden; declaration in .subscribers .word takes priority over the visibility: visible; declaration in .subscribers .word:before, even though the latter should be able to set its own rules.

Luckily, there is an alternative method that works in all modern browsers.

How to Change the Terms

Final Code

.subscribers .word {
 display: none;
}
.subscribers .number:after {
 content: " Pikachus";
}
.users-online .word {
 display: none;
}
.users-online .number:after {
 content: " Pichus lost now";
}

The Process

Step 1: Hiding 'subscribers' and 'users here now'

First, we must divide and concur. Our first target is the words we want eliminated: 'subscribers' and 'users here now'. We've already put together the code explosive, so your task is to sneak it into enemy headquarters, set the charge, and get out there alive. Good luck.

.subscribers .word {
 display: none;
}
.users-online .word {
 display: none;
}

Step 2: Adding Your Own Terms

I've got good news. While you were fending off hostiles, we set your tracker on the offensive and opened up a direct connection to their servers, which were surprisingly unencrypted with no firewall. They must be paying their techs minimum wage. Anyway, now that we have a direct link to their database, we need to upload this code:

.subscribers .number:after {
 content: " Pikachus";
}
.users-online .number:after {
 content: " Pichus lost now";
}

We've put a space before the terms to make sure the quantity and the descriptor retain their separation so that the enemy will be unaware of any changes. The connection is still live, so if you think our trained professionals have made a mistake in what terms to use, feel free to change them.
